Gauge Chart

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/gauge-charts.Rmd
gauge-charts.Rmd

Basic Gauge

A radial gauge chart has a circular arc, which displays a single value to estimate progress toward a goal. The bar shows the target value, and the shading represents the progress toward that goal. Gauge charts, known as speedometer charts as well. This chart type is usually used to illustrate key business indicators.

The example below displays a basic gauge chart with default attributes.

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_indicator(
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),
    value = 270,
    title = go_indicator_title(text = "Speed"),
    mode = "gauge+number"
  ) |>
  update_layout(margin = go_margin(l = 20, r = 30))

fig

Add Steps, Threshold, and Delta

The following examples include “steps” attribute shown as shading inside the radial arc, “delta” which is the difference of the value and goal (reference - value), and “threshold” to determine boundaries that visually alert you if the value cross a defined threshold.

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_indicator(
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),
    value = 450,
    title = go_indicator_title(text = "Speed"),
    mode = "gauge+number+delta",
    delta = go_indicator_delta(reference = 380),
    gauge = go_indicator_gauge(
      axis = go_indicator_gauge_axis(range = list(NULL, 500)),
      steps = list(
        go_indicator_gauge_step(range = c(0, 250), color = "lightgray"),
        go_indicator_gauge_step(range = c(250, 400), color = "gray")
      ),
      threshold = go_indicator_gauge_threshold(
        line = go_indicator_gauge_threshold_line(color = "red", width = 4),
        thickness = 0.75,
        value = 490
      )
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(margin = go_margin(l = 20, r = 30))

fig

Custom Gauge Chart

The following example shows how to style your gauge charts. For more information about all possible options see go_indicator().

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_indicator(
    mode = "gauge+number+delta",
    value = 420,
    title = go_indicator_title(text = "Speed", font = go_font(size = 24)),
    delta = go_indicator_delta(
      reference = 400,
      increasing = go_indicator_delta_increasing(color = "RebeccaPurple")
    ),
    gauge = go_indicator_gauge(
      axis = go_indicator_gauge_axis(
        range = list(NULL, 500),
        tickwidth = 1,
        tickcolor = "darkblue"
      ),
      bar = go_indicator_gauge_bar(color = "darkblue"),
      bgcolor = "white",
      borderwidth = 2,
      bordercolor = "gray",
      steps = list(
        go_indicator_gauge_step(range = c(0, 250), color = "cyan"),
        go_indicator_gauge_step(range = c(250, 400), color = "royalblue")
      ),
      threshold = go_indicator_gauge_threshold(
        line = go_indicator_gauge_threshold_line(color = "red", width = 4),
        thickness = 0.75,
        value = 490
      )
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    margin = go_margin(l = 20, r = 30),
    paper_bgcolor = "lavender",
    font = go_font(color = "darkblue", family = "Arial")
  )

fig

See go_indicator() for more information and chart attribute options!
